item.text: {"facts":[{"source_id":"SRC-1c8893883494669e","start_unit":24,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"In February 2023, the Scholz coalition introduced a bill to accelerate smart-meter deployment, with binding rollout targets through 2030, mandatory installation from 2025 for households using over 6,000 kWh annually or having photovoltaic systems above 7 kW, and privacy requirements covering storage, deletion, and anonymization.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"2023 policy proposal with implementation targets extending to 2030","ruler_attribution":"Scholz federal coalition and its parliamentary groups","limitations":["The source describes the bill and intended rollout, not completed implementation or outcomes."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1c8893883494669e","start_unit":29,"end_unit":31,"fact_summary":"At the March 2023 public hearing, experts supported faster smart-meter deployment in principle but identified unresolved problems involving calibration law, unnecessary installation costs and electronic waste, social distribution of dynamic tariffs, detailed household-use data, limited gateway capacity, insufficiently prepared metering operators, and uncertain cost recovery.","question_ids":["1B.9","5B.4","5B.7","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023 expert findings during legislative review","ruler_attribution":"Parliamentary experts evaluating the coalition bill","limitations":["These are expert assessments, not an official finding that the coalition corrected each issue."]},{"source_id":"SRC-1c8893883494669e","start_unit":34,"end_unit":37,"fact_summary":"On 20 April 2023, the Bundestag passed the amended smart-meter law; it removed the prior BSI approval requirement while retaining the secure gateway framework and adding detailed data-storage, deletion, and anonymization rules, with a 2030 rollout objective.","question_ids":["1B.9","5B.6","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Enacted in April 2023","ruler_attribution":"Scholz coalition government and Bundestag majority","limitations":["The source records enactment and design, not later compliance or measurable effects."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5f243bf2f772b9e0","start_unit":4,"end_unit":8,"fact_summary":"The 2023/24 Council of Economic Experts reported that Germany's output was near its pre-pandemic level, with the weakest growth in the euro area since the pandemic; extensive energy-supply and crisis-mitigation measures prevented a deeper downturn, but long-term growth constraints had not been adequately addressed.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.7","5B.9","5B.10","8B.7"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Assessment published during 2023 covering current and long-term conditions","ruler_attribution":"Independent Council of Economic Experts assessing Germany under the Scholz government","limitations":["The report attributes the weak long-term position to developments extending beyond 2023 and does not assign all causality to Scholz."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5f243bf2f772b9e0","start_unit":15,"end_unit":17,"fact_summary":"The Council forecast German GDP to contract by 0.4 percent in 2023 and average inflation to reach 6.1 percent, while inflation fell from 8.7 percent year-on-year in January to 4.5 percent in September.","question_ids":["5B.3","5B.9","5B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023 forecast and January–September 2023 results","ruler_attribution":"Independent Council of Economic Experts","limitations":["The figures describe national outcomes and do not establish that government policy caused them."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5f243bf2f772b9e0","start_unit":26,"end_unit":28,"fact_summary":"The Council found that lower-income household net incomes had stagnated relative to average real incomes and that poverty risk had increased; it identified particularly high exposure among single parents, unemployed people, children, young people, and people with migration backgrounds, while noting that proposed basic-security and childcare reforms could improve incentives and reduce poverty.","question_ids":["5B.8","6B.2","6B.3","6B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Longitudinal finding presented in the 2023/24 report","ruler_attribution":"Independent Council of Economic Experts","limitations":["The source reports distributional conditions and reform options, not their implementation by Scholz in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-5f243bf2f772b9e0","start_unit":32,"end_unit":34,"fact_summary":"The Council found Germany's research-data infrastructure remained internationally backward, with insufficient timely data and weak data access and linkage; it noted that during the COVID-19 and energy crises policies could not be evaluated alongside implementation as readily as in France or the United States.","question_ids":["5B.7","8B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Institutional assessment in the 2023/24 report","ruler_attribution":"Independent Council of Economic Experts","limitations":["The report mentions initiatives under way but does not establish that the proposed reforms were enacted in 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-42a395030302baf9","start_unit":24,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"In October 2023, the federal government proposed requiring all municipalities to produce heat plans, with deadlines of January 2026 for cities over 100,000 residents and June 2028 for smaller municipalities, backed by 500 million euros in federal funding.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","6B.1","8B.1","8B.2"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Government bill introduced in October 2023","ruler_attribution":"Scholz federal government","limitations":["The source describes a proposal before final enactment."]},{"source_id":"SRC-42a395030302baf9","start_unit":30,"end_unit":33,"fact_summary":"October 2023 experts broadly supported municipal heat planning as a strategic instrument but warned that deadlines, staffing, data-collection duties, hydrogen assumptions, financing, and coordination with the building-energy law could create excessive bureaucracy, delays, or implementation failure; the environmental organization DUH said the proposed 2030 renewable-heat target was too low and difficult to reconcile with climate goals.","question_ids":["5B.7","5B.9","6B.5","8B.8"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Expert evidence during 2023 legislative review","ruler_attribution":"Parliamentary experts evaluating the government proposal","limitations":["The source records competing expert views rather than a later implementation audit."]},{"source_id":"SRC-42a395030302baf9","start_unit":40,"end_unit":43,"fact_summary":"On 17 November 2023, the Bundestag passed the municipal heat-planning law, requiring state-level heat planning, 50 percent climate-neutral networked heat by 2030, renewable or unavoidable-waste heat shares of at least 30 percent by 2030 and 80 percent by 2040 in existing networks, and full renewable or waste-heat operation by the end of 2044.","question_ids":["5B.1","5B.6","6B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Enacted in November 2023 with future implementation deadlines","ruler_attribution":"Scholz coalition government and Bundestag majority","limitations":["The law's future outcomes and municipal capacity were contested in the same source."]},{"source_id":"SRC-60a3eb49fd3d4236","start_unit":24,"end_unit":24,"fact_summary":"In September 2023, the federal government proposed an amendment to the Online Access Act to institutionalize federal-state cooperation, provide central citizen-account and mailbox services, introduce qualified electronic seals, and permit digital-only procedures for business services.","question_ids":["5B.6","8B.1","8B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"Government proposal introduced in September 2023","ruler_attribution":"Scholz federal government","limitations":["The source records a proposal and referral to committees, not completed 2023 implementation."]},{"source_id":"SRC-60a3eb49fd3d4236","start_unit":33,"end_unit":36,"fact_summary":"At the October 2023 hearing, experts reported that only 105 of the 575 services targeted for online access by the end of 2022 were online at the previous year-end and agreed that the original Online Access Act had missed its target; they also found the 2023 amendment insufficient, citing absent standards, timelines, cost clarity, independent monitoring, security rules, and a common technical model.","question_ids":["5B.6","5B.7","8B.5","8B.6","8B.8"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"2023 implementation assessment and hearing","ruler_attribution":"Independent experts assessing the federal government's digital-administration programme","limitations":["The implementation shortfall began under the 2017 law and is not solely attributable to Scholz."]},{"source_id":"SRC-60a3eb49fd3d4236","start_unit":38,"end_unit":38,"fact_summary":"The Bundestag's later account states that the Online Access Act amendment was not finally approved until February 2024, so the 2023 government proposal had not become enacted federal law by the end of 2023.","question_ids":["8B.6","8B.10"],"polarity":"adverse","period_fit":"Procedural status of a 2023 proposal established by subsequent parliamentary record","ruler_attribution":"Federal legislative process under the Scholz government","limitations":["The final enactment occurred outside the target period."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e331caeaae44d885","start_unit":2,"end_unit":3,"fact_summary":"The 2023 human-rights report found no reports of government or agent arbitrary killings, disappearances, political prisoners, or credible official torture; it also found that authorities generally respected arrest safeguards and judicial independence, while noting some human-rights groups considered police-mistreatment investigations ineffective and lacking an independent mechanism.","question_ids":["3B.1","3B.2","3B.4","3B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Country assessment for 2023","ruler_attribution":"German federal and state authorities under the Scholz government","limitations":["Some findings concern state authorities outside the federal government's direct control."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e331caeaae44d885","start_unit":5,"end_unit":6,"fact_summary":"The government generally did not restrict internet access or censor online content without legal authority, but it permitted removal of websites of banned organizations and content involving racial hatred, Nazism, or Holocaust denial; authorities also monitored extremist-associated websites and social-media accounts.","question_ids":["3B.5","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Country assessment for 2023","ruler_attribution":"German government and security authorities","limitations":["The report does not identify a specific 2023 federal order for each restriction."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e331caeaae44d885","start_unit":5,"end_unit":7,"fact_summary":"Authorities generally respected peaceful assembly but used preventive detention, rally bans, and forceful police tactics in some cases; climate activists reported painful tactics during street-clearance operations, and Amnesty criticized increasing restrictions on assembly.","question_ids":["3B.8","3B.9","4B.3"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Country assessment for 2023","ruler_attribution":"German state and local authorities operating within the federal system","limitations":["Several incidents were state or municipal matters rather than decisions personally directed by Scholz."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e331caeaae44d885","start_unit":9,"end_unit":11,"fact_summary":"The report found that Germany generally enforced laws against rape and domestic violence and supported gender-violence prevention, but shelters lacked approximately 15,000 places nationwide and had no open spaces on 303 days in 2022; it also reported persistent gender pay disparities and underfunding or insufficient independence of anti-discrimination bodies.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023 country report using 2022 service and wage data","ruler_attribution":"German federal, state, and local institutions","limitations":["Some quantitative indicators predate 2023 and the report does not attribute the gaps specifically to Scholz."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e331caeaae44d885","start_unit":11,"end_unit":12,"fact_summary":"In 2023, the federal Demokratie Leben programme distributed 182 million euros to organizations promoting diversity and combating extremism; meanwhile, the 2022 record included 20,967 right-wing politically motivated crimes, including 1,016 violent crimes, and antisemitic crimes increased during 2023.","question_ids":["3B.3","3B.7","3B.9","6B.3"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023 funding and 2022/2023 violence indicators","ruler_attribution":"German federal government and security institutions","limitations":["Crime totals cited for right-wing extremism are from 2022, while the antisemitism trend is described for 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e331caeaae44d885","start_unit":14,"end_unit":14,"fact_summary":"In June 2023, the Bundestag passed a law doubling the maximum monthly fine for employers failing to meet disability-employment quotas from 360 to 720 euros beginning in 2024, while the report found accessibility requirements for health care, public information, housing, and employment were not consistently met.","question_ids":["3B.7","6B.3","6B.8","8B.2"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Law enacted in 2023 with implementation from 2024","ruler_attribution":"Scholz coalition and Bundestag","limitations":["The source does not provide evidence of the law's later enforcement effect."]},{"source_id":"SRC-e331caeaae44d885","start_unit":15,"end_unit":16,"fact_summary":"The government effectively enforced labor, minimum-wage, working-time, and occupational-safety rules; the Customs Office's illicit-work unit checked nearly 53,100 businesses in 2022, and the enforcement system had approximately 8,600 investigators.","question_ids":["5B.4","5B.6","6B.2","8B.6"],"polarity":"favorable","period_fit":"2023 report using latest available 2022 enforcement data","ruler_attribution":"German federal labor and customs authorities","limitations":["The quantitative enforcement data are for 2022 rather than 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-f4fceff840a9a9c3","start_unit":13,"end_unit":13,"fact_summary":"The Federal Employment Agency reported that in 2023 average unemployment rose by 191,000 to 2.609 million and underemployment rose by 264,000 to 3.449 million, while social-insurance employment increased by 264,000 to 34.71 million between June 2022 and June 2023; the increase was entirely due to foreign employment.","question_ids":["5B.8","5B.9","5B.10","6B.10"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"Annual labor-market results for 2023","ruler_attribution":"National labor-market outcome during the Scholz government","limitations":["The figures do not establish causal responsibility for the government."]},{"source_id":"SRC-df97fe6adc3a48e8","start_unit":3,"end_unit":5,"fact_summary":"Freedom House rated Germany's internet environment Free at 77/100, with independent judicial oversight and generally strong political rights, but noted that the government had struggled to provide high-speed access to every household; fiber access reached 26 percent in 2022 and 93 percent of households had speeds above 50 Mbps.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.4","4B.6","5B.6"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023 country assessment using mainly 2022 infrastructure data","ruler_attribution":"German state and regulatory framework under the Scholz coalition","limitations":["Most infrastructure figures predate 2023 and the report covers June 2022–May 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-df97fe6adc3a48e8","start_unit":24,"end_unit":26,"fact_summary":"Freedom House found that German online-content restrictions generally met minimum transparency, proportionality, and appeal requirements, but also recorded criticism that the Federal Network Agency's role in private DNS blocking for copyright could normalize network blocking and was not designed to assess fundamental rights.","question_ids":["4B.3","4B.6","4B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023 internet-freedom assessment","ruler_attribution":"German regulatory framework and Federal Network Agency","limitations":["The copyright-blocking mechanism largely predates 2023."]},{"source_id":"SRC-df97fe6adc3a48e8","start_unit":42,"end_unit":49,"fact_summary":"In March 2023, German parliamentary experts broadly criticized proposed EU chat-control measures as threatening privacy; a January 2023 Interior Ministry draft excluded client-side scanning but retained surveillance of non-encrypted communications, while Justice Ministry proposals would enable platforms to provide IP addresses in broadly defined online-violence cases.","question_ids":["1B.9","3B.5","4B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023 legislative and expert debate","ruler_attribution":"Scholz coalition ministries and parliamentary experts","limitations":["The material concerns proposals and Germany's position in an EU process, not a completed 2023 law."]},{"source_id":"SRC-df97fe6adc3a48e8","start_unit":49,"end_unit":52,"fact_summary":"Freedom House reported that Germany's intelligence and police laws permitted extensive surveillance capabilities, including malware and broad communications collection, while noting that in February 2023 the Constitutional Court invalidated parts of police data-mining and surveillance laws for lacking sufficiently specific conditions and requiring concrete threats.","question_ids":["3B.4","3B.5","4B.4","4B.9"],"polarity":"mixed","period_fit":"2023 report and February 2023 court findings","ruler_attribution":"German legislature, executive security bodies, and constitutional courts","limitations":["Many surveillance powers originated before 2023 and were distributed across federal and state systems."]}],"documents_with_no_material_fact":["SRC-62a5c4d126eca104"],"batch_limitations":["The supplied sources provide institutional, legislative, and outcome evidence; they rarely document Olaf Scholz's personal statements, appointments, or direct decisions.","Several sources report proposals, expert criticism, or outcomes without establishing individual causal responsibility by Scholz.","Some documents include later procedural developments or pre-2023 figures; records identify those temporal limitations explicitly."]}
